steps.text: Whisk together honey, vinegar, olive oil, lemon juice, Worcestershire sauce, tarragon, rosemary, garlic powder, white pepper, and salt in a large bowl until well combined; pour into a resealable plastic bag. Add flat iron steak; coat with marinade, squeeze out excess air, and seal the bag. Place in the refrigerator to marinate for at least 6 hours.
Preheat an outdoor grill for medium-high heat and lightly oil the grate.

Remove steak from marinade; shake off excess and discard marinade. Cook steak on the preheated grill to desired degree of doneness, about 4 minutes per side for medium-rare. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center of steak should read 140 degrees F (60 degrees C) for medium-rare doneness.

raw_recipe.headline: Marinated Flat Iron Steak
raw_recipe.description: This easy marinade for flat iron steak is made with honey, balsamic vinegar, olive oil, lemon juice, Worcestershire, garlic, dried herbs, and spices.

review.reviewBody: Very good marinade for a tasy cut of beef. For those sayin the flat iron is too tough you must be cutting it incorrectly. Try cutting in 1/4" strips ACROSS the grain. This makes a world of difference. Use fresh roasted and smashed garlic instead of garlic powder.

This is a GREAT marinade recipe!! I marinaded it overnight in a plastic bag then seared on a hot cast iron griddle on my gas grill. Once it was seared, I finished it in a 400 degree oven to 130 degrees. This is the same way I make any cut of steak. I know the best steak houses make steak this way, so I highly recommend it.

Great marinade that hits all 4 taste centers in your mouth (sweet, sour, salt, bitter)! The Flat Iron steak cooked Medium Rare is hard to beat for flavor and tenderness. I prefer to tenderize it even more with a Jaccard 3-row meat tenderizer. Use the marinade recipe above, throw it and the meat in a 9X9" pyrex baking dish and then use the tenderizer to infuse the marinade deep into the meat and help cut through the connective tissues. Cook 4 minutes on the first side, 6 minutes on the flip side and then remove from the grill and wrap with tin-foil for 5 to 10 minutes to let the juices reabsorb. Do not overcook this cut of beef, the thicker end will come out Medium Rare while the thinner end comes out Medium. Cut across the grain in 1/8" to 1/4" strips and watch the meat disappear. This same method works well for Flank Steak but pound for pound dollar-wise, nothing beats the Flat Iron for taste and tenderness. Thanks for the great marinade!

Excellent flavor! Enhanced original recipe after reading some reviews regarding lack of tenderness...
Super Secret: Be sure to tenderize the meat by banging with a meat tenderizer on both sides and sprinkling both sides with a meat tenderizer with no MSG. Then I added the two steaks into the plastic baggie and let it marinate in the fridge for approximately three hours. Will definitely use again.

Yes, this marinade is much sweeter than most. But I liked it. Instead of grilling the steak, I cut the marinated (overnight) meat in strips and pan fried in the marinade. Served with rice and a simple salad of baby greens and grape tomatoes for a very delicious meal. (There were a few steak strips left over from the first meal and I sauteed red bell pepper and onions, added some oregano, and the meat for very tasty fajitas.)

Worked fine with reducing the honey to 2 Tbs. Substitued black for white pepper and used minced fresh garlic instead of powder. Also marinated overnight for dinner next day, so the meat was tender and tasty.
No changes - I let it marinate for 24 hours, and it was SO tender, juicy and flavorful!

Worked fine with reducing the honey to 2 Tbs. Substitued black for white pepper and used minced fresh garlic instead of powder. Also marinated overnight for dinner next day, so the meat was tender and tasty.

Delicious! I marinate for a good 24 hours. I think th ehoney and balsamic giv eit great flavor. I've even used this for a giant chuck steak and threw everything along with some potatoes, carrots, onion and stock into a crock pot and made a kind of pot roast out of it.

I had no honey so used molasses instead. Also used fresh minced garlic instead of powder, and white balsamic vinegar instead of regular. My olive oil was a dipping oil with wild mushrooms and sage. Ok, so I guess I made a lot of changes and just used the recipe for proportions. Delicious.

Flat Iron steak has become very popular and is no longer an inexpensive meat where I am at (Denver). You are lucky to find it on sale for the price top sirloin steak. Good marinade recipe, I tried it on 3/4" thick boneless chuck steak, and it turned out very well. I used twice the amount of fresh tarragon and fresh rosemary, and added some chopped basil, and used 2 cloves of garlic, minced instead of dried.
I used this on a tres major cut and it tasted weird. The tarragon should not be in the mix, basil would be better choice.
I only used the marinade in this recipe and it was delicious.

Well this site won’t let me upload the photo, but this marinade really made the steak. We cooked it slowly on the grill which gave it a nice char and tenderness. Served with Bulgarian potato salad and caprese salad with balsamic which coupled really nicely.
Didn't give meat much flavor even when marinated for 6 hrs. Hubs made himself hot dogs. Deleting from my recipe box.
Made exactly as stated and it was delicious! Meat came out very tender. I will be making this again!

I only had time to marinate for an hour and it was still fantastic. My husband loved it and even my 7 yr old liked it. The second time I didn't have balsamic vinegar so I used apple cider vinegar and it was still great.
Excellent marinade. Doubled the recipe for 2.25 lb's of steak. Also used fresh garlic instead of powder. Will be adding this to our top 10 steak dishes. Thanks.
Very tender a little sweet for me, less honey next time
This is our favorite marinade for steak!! Delicious .
